title: What protects turbine blades from scorching steam?

segments.text: What protects turbine blades from scorching steam?
A major challenge facing turbine design is reducing creep experienced by the blades.
To limit creep, thermal coatings and superalloys with solid‑solution strengthening and grain‑boundary strengthening are used in blade designs.
Protective coatings, often stabilized zirconium‑dioxide‑based ceramics, reduce thermal damage and limit oxidation.
Nickel‑based blades are alloyed with aluminum and titanium, forming a gamma‑prime phase that improves strength and creep resistance.
These materials help blades endure high‑temperature steam environments without losing performance.
